parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station Opiro (Etche LGA survey stations). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 54.639 | 0.2147 | 0.2147
2 | 9147.8 | 0.30305 | 0.51774
3 | 1119.9 | 21.107 | 21.625
4 | 2566.8 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as A-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Station: Opiro
Curve type: KH-type — the resistivity sequence (54.6 → 9147.8 → 1119.9 → 2566.8 Ω·m, i.e. ρ1<ρ2>ρ3<ρ4) shows a rise-fall-rise pattern typical of a KH curve, not the monotonically increasing pattern required for an A-type curve. The file's "A-type" label appears to be a data-entry/interpretation error and should be re-checked against the raw sounding curve.
Aquifer depth: ≈ 0.52 m – 21.63 m (Layer 3, ρ ≈ 1119.9 Ω·m, thickness ≈ 21.1 m — the most likely saturated, permeable horizon given its moderate resistivity and substantial thickness relative to the thin, very high-resistivity Layer 2 above and the higher-resistivity Layer 4 below).
Recommendation: Target the screen interval within approximately 0.5–21.6 m depth, corresponding to the moderate-resistivity Layer 3, and confirm formation lithology with drill cuttings before setting screens. Before finalizing the borehole design, flag the curve-type discrepancy to the interpretation team, as correct classification affects confidence in aquifer continuity and depth-to-basement estimates at this station.
